content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've noticed an issue with user web pages on [product_name] [version_no]. When I enter the device IP address directly in the browser's navigation bar (for example, 192.168.1.111 and press ENTER), I receive a '404: Target is not found' error, and the navigation bar displays '192.168.1.111/lfs/dev/sdcard/webroot/login.htm'. However, if I use the address '192.168.1.111/logo_login.shtm?!App-Language=1', I can access the standard web page and then log in to the customized site successfully. If I remove the microSD card from [product_name], using only the IP address to access works, and after reinserting the microSD, I can get to the custom site. This behavior seems to happen mostly with complex or 'heavy' custom web pages. Simpler pages with just a few buttons work as expected. I tested both deploying directly to microSD and downloading via Ethernet — the result stays the same. I've used different browsers (IE, Microsoft Edge, Chrome) with identical outcomes. Can anyone explain why this is happening? Thank you in advance for your assistance. Best regards from Madrid, [user_name]
Could you please upload your [document] project and [product_name] program?

Here’s a suggestion: Disconnect the Ethernet cable from [product_name]. On your PC, open a command prompt and run: ping <device IP address>. If you receive a response, it means another device is using that same IP address on your network. To resolve this, configure your router's DHCP range so the device IP address is outside of DHCP assignments. Some routers don’t fully separate DHCP devices from those with static IPs. Hope this helps.
Hello [user_name], I've attached the [document] and [document] program. Thanks again for your help.

Also, when trying to access the web page without Wi-Fi (disabled) and only connecting my laptop and the device by Ethernet, I have the same issue — I can reach the web page using '192.168.1.111/logo_login.shtm?!App-Language=1', but not by entering '192.168.1.111' alone. Thanks for your help, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that accessing custom webpages on [product_name] [version_no] by entering the device’s IP address causes a '404: Target is not found' error. When the full path is entered, access works as expected. The issue appears with more complex web pages and doesn’t occur with simpler ones. It’s reproducible across various browsers, unrelated to IP conflicts, and doesn’t affect previous versions, where peers were unable to reproduce the problem.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to access their custom web pages directly via device IP address, regardless of page complexity or deployment method, similar to previous versions and standard web pages.
